summary: Peter Giles was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1878–1882) and Gonville and Caius College (~1882–1887). He was Cambridge's Reader in Comparative Philology (~1891–1935) and Emmanuel College's Fellow, Lecturer (~1890–1911), and Master (~1911–1935).

Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Peter Harvey founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996. He was attested between 2002 and 2015 as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Sunderland.
Peter Haskel works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He pursued graduate studies at Columbia University, where he studied under Yoshito S. Hakeda.

Peter J. Wilson earned his Ph.D. at Yale University (~1956–1961) and taught there, at Vassar College, and at the University of Washington. He later held teaching posts at Bennington College (~1968–1971) and the University of Otago (~1971–1998).

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Peter James Gilks studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and completed a PhD under John Powers at the Australian National University (attested 2010). His teachers also included Geshe Ngawang Jangchup and Geshe Thubten Wangchen.
Peter K. Austin is a linguist who studied at the Australian National University from 1975 to 1978. He later held a post at SOAS University of London from around 2002 to 2018.

Peter Koret, a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields, completed his doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London. He subsequently held posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

Peter Kuhlmann is a linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Rosemarie Lühr (~1990–1993). He held academic posts at the University of Giessen (~1994–1999), the University of Düsseldorf (~1999–2004), and the University of Göttingen (~2004).

Peter M. Scharf, working in Indology, linguistics, and computational fields, completed his dissertation under George Cardona at the University of Pennsylvania. He held a post at Brown University (2006–2009) and served as President of the Sanskrit Library (attested 2014, 2024–2025).
Peter Masefield is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his studies under the supervision of L. P. N. Perera and Ninian Smart (attested 1986).

Peter Moran, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied at Tufts University and completed a PhD at the University of Washington under Charles F. Keyes. His instructors included Geshe Nawang Lhundrup Nornang, Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, and Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche.

Peter N. Gregory specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology, completing his Ph.D. at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi (1981). He served as Executive Director and editor at the Kuroda Institute, and taught at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and Smith College.
Peter Peterson was an Indologist. From around 1873 to 1899, he served as Bombay Professor / Sanskrit Professor at Elphinstone College and as a professor at the University of Mumbai.

Indologist Peter Schreiner earned degrees from Temple, Münster (under Paul Hacker, ~1970–1972), and Tübingen (Habilitation). He held posts at Tübingen (1974–1982), SOAS (1988), and the University of Zurich as professor (1990) and professor emeritus (~2009).
Peter Schwabland is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA at the University of Washington under the supervision of Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.

Tibetologist Peter Schwieger studied at the University of Bonn under Dieter Schuh, earning his doctorate (-1982) and habilitation (-1995). He worked at the Göttingen Academy (1978), held a guest professorship at Humboldt University (2001), and gained Bonn's Tibetology chair in 2001.

Peter Skilling is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who earned his PhD from EPHE under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub (-2004). He founded and directed the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation and held posts at EFEO (2007, 2009) and Chulalongkorn University.

Peter Stewart is an art historian and Indologist who studied at Clare College, Cambridge (~1992–1998). He held posts at Cambridge, Reading, the Courtauld Institute of Art, Wolfson College, and Oxford, where he became Associate Professor of Classical Art and Archaeology (2011).

Peter Zieme works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Humboldt University (1960–1965), he held posts at the GDR Academy (1965–2007), Berlin-Brandenburg Academy (~1969–2007), and as honorary professor at Freie Universität Berlin (~1994).

Peter van der Veer studied at Groningen (~1972–1979) and Utrecht (~1979–1986). In religious studies and Indology, his posts included professor at the University of Amsterdam (1992), University of Pennsylvania (~1992–2000), and director at the Max Planck Institute (~2008–2021).
